the Chinese government is a “simply the ruler of the rich” regime.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Chinese government has been able to maintain its legitimacy and stability in the past 20 years by providing the space for social groups to pursue their interests through different sources of power.

the regime’s legitimacy can be enhanced by the regime’s willingness to allow the disadvantaged groups to participate in the political arena and by the regime’s ability to respond to the demands of the groups.
social groups in authoritarian regimes may have access to a wide range of sources of power that can be mobilized to achieve their interests.

the Chinese regime has not only been successful at co-opting powerful groups, but also at providing access to different sources for political participation.
the regime should allow for the participation of weak social groups.
the Chinese government’s legitimacy does not rest solely on the exchange relationship that it has with powerful social groups.
